sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 353.

PD 353.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 353 was established by Ordinance No. 21337, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 24, 1992. Ordinance No. 21337 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Ordinance No. 21337 was amended by Ordinance No. 21976, passed by the Dallas City Council on February 23, 1994. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 21337; 21976; 25850)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 353 is established on property generally located at the northwest corner of Inwood Road and Willow Lane. The size of PD 353 is approximately 27.18 acres. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A. (Ord. 25850)

SEC. 51P-353.103.1. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 353A: conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit 353B: detailed development plan.

(3) Exhibit 353C: landscape plan.

(4) Exhibit 353D: traffic management plan. (Ord. 31018)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.104. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Use and development of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 353A). In the event of a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 21976; 25850)

sections.title: Detailed Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.105. DETAILED DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development on the Property must comply with the detailed development plan (Exhibit 353B). A detailed development plan for subsequent phases of development on the Property must be submitted to and approved by the city plan commission prior to the issuance of any building permit for expansion of an existing structure, or for construction of any new structure on the Property. Any detailed development plan must comply with the conceptual plan. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)

sections.title: Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.106. USES.

(a) In general. Only the following uses are permitted on the Property.

(1) Private school. For purposes of this article, private school includes recreation areas and athletic facilities, limited to playgrounds, parks, game courts, swimming pools, and playing fields. [Additional restrictions on outdoor recreation and athletic facilities are contained in Subsection (c).]

(2) Single family residential uses.

(b) Uses permitted by zone. Only the following uses are permitted in the zones indicated.

ZONE USES PERMITTED

B-1, B-2, and B-3 Classrooms, administration offices, indoor recreational and athletic facilities, faculty residences, food service facilities, arts and cultural facilities, auditoriums, library, research facilities, and parking.

P Parking.

A-1, A-4, and A-5 Outdoor recreation area and athletic facilities limited to game courts, swimming pools, playgrounds, athletic fields, stadium seating, press facilities, restrooms, concession stands, ticket booths, maintenance buildings, and light standards.

A-2 Two light standards.

A-3 Playground.

A-P All uses permitted in Zones A-1 and P.

(c) Additional provisions for certain uses.

(1) Football stadium. Any amendment which would increase the height or seating capacity of the football stadium must comply with the zoning amendment procedures for a change in zoning district classification, and must be reflected in the conceptual plan and planned development conditions governing the Property.

(2) Tennis courts.

(A) No tennis courts located on the western one-half of the Property may be lighted.

(B) Where lighting of outdoor tennis courts is permitted, all lighting must be shown on the approved development plan and must include the location and height of light poles or standards and type of lights to be used. The tennis court lighting must be adjusted so as not to produce glare that creates a traffic hazard on streets adjacent to the Property.

(3) Outdoor athletic facilities. The following restrictions apply to the use of all outdoor athletic facilities on the Property:

(A) No amplified sound is permitted from 11:00 p.m. through 8:00 a.m.

(B) Exterior lights may be illuminated only on Friday and Saturday and any two additional nights each week, except that tennis court lighting, where permitted, may be illuminated every night of the week.

(C) Exterior lights are permitted until 11:00 p.m. for football games and until 10:30 p.m. for all other authorized outdoor athletic activities.

(D) During the days and hours when exterior lights are authorized under Paragraphs (B) and (C), the outdoor athletic facilities may only be used by groups 19 years of age or younger; and by alumni groups, parents’ groups, students, or faculty of the school located on the Property. Except as expressly provided in this article or the Dallas Development Code, there is no limitation on use of the outdoor facilities by alumni groups, parents’ groups, students, or faculty of the school located on the Property.

(E) Only amateur groups are allowed to use the outdoor athletic facilities.

(F) Nonprofit amateur groups other than those described in Paragraph
(D) may use the outdoor athletic facilities for special events provided the following requirements are satisfied:

(i) No more than six special events are permitted each year.

(ii) The use of the outdoor athletic facilities is restricted to the hours from 9:00 a.m. through 7:00 p.m.

(4) Natatorium.

(A) The natatorium in Zone B-1, as shown on the detailed development plan, is not available for public use.

(B) The natatorium may only be used by the following:

(i) the faculty, students, and alumni of the private school on the Property;

(ii) participants in sports camps or other events sponsored by the private school on the Property or its coaches;

(iii) students attending private schools within a four-mile radius of the private school on the Property;

students from other private or public schools who are engaged in athletic practices or competitions with the students of the private school on the Property; and coaches and spectators at any athletic practices or competitions, sports camps, or other allowed events sponsored by the private school on the Property. (Ord. Nos. 21976; 25850; 31018)

sections.title: Development Standards For Residential Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.107. DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS FOR RESIDENTIAL USES.

The development standards applicable to the R-16(A) Single Family District, as provided in Chapter 51A, apply to single family residential uses on the Property. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)

sections.title: Maximum Floor Area
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.108. MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA.

Maximum floor area in Zones B-1, B-2, and B-3 combined is 390,000 square feet. Maximum floor area in Zones A-1, A-4, A-5, A-P, and P combined is 15,000 square feet. No floor area is allowed in Zone A-2 or A-3. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850; 31018)

sections.title: Residential Proximity Slope
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.110. RESIDENTIAL PROXIMITY SLOPE.

(a) The residential proximity slope applies to structures on the Property as follows:

(1) The slope applies to all structures except those described in Paragraph (2).

(2) The slope does not apply to:

(A) structures in Zones B-1, B-2, and B-3; and

(B) the three light standards and the stadium seating on the west side of the football stadium.

(b) This PD is considered to be a residential zoning district for purposes of determining the applicability of residential proximity slope regulations which restrict the heights of structures on property adjacent to this PD. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)

sections.title: Lot Coverage
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.111. LOT COVERAGE.

Maximum lot coverage on the Property is 290,000 square feet. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850; 31018)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.113. OFF-STREET PARKING.

(a) Parking is permitted only in Zones P, A-P, B-1, B-2, and B-3, and in the setback area adjacent to the western and northern boundaries of the Property.

(b) Consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(c) A special parking license is not required for remote parking located within PD 983, south of Willow Lane and within 1,500 feet walking distance from the main northeast entrance of the private school located on the Property.

(d) All off-street parking must either be surface parking or be located below grade. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850; 31018)

SEC.51P-353.113.1. TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN.

(a) In general. Operation of a private school must comply with the traffic management plan (Exhibit 353D).

(b) Queuing. Queuing is only permitted inside the Property. Student drop-off and pick-up are not permitted within city rights-of-way.

(c) Traffic study.

(1) The Property owner or operator shall prepare a traffic study evaluating the sufficiency of the traffic management plan. The initial traffic study must be submitted to the director by November 1, 2020. After the initial traffic study, the Property owner or operator shall submit annual updates of the traffic study to the director by November 1st of each even- numbered year.

(2) The traffic study must be in writing, performed by a licensed engineer, based on a minimum of four samples taken on different school days at different drop-off and pick-up times over a two-week period, and must contain an analysis of the following:

(A) ingress and egress points;

(B) queue lengths;

(C) number and location of personnel assisting with loading and unloading of students;

(D) drop-off and pick-up locations;

(E) drop-off and pick-up hours for each grade level;

(F) hours for each grade level; and

(G) circulation.
(3) Within 30 days after submission of a traffic study, the director shall determine if the current traffic management plan is sufficient.

(A) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan is sufficient, the director shall notify the applicant in writing.

(B) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan results in traffic hazards or traffic congestion, the director shall require the Property owner to submit an amended traffic management plan. If the Property owner fails to submit an amended traffic management plan within 30 days, the director shall notify the city plan commission.

(d) Amendment process.

(1) A traffic management plan may be amended using minor plan amendment fee and public hearing process in Section 51A-1.105(k)(3).

(2) The city plan commission shall authorize changes in a traffic management plan if the proposed amendments improve queuing or traffic circulation; eliminate traffic hazards; or decrease traffic congestion. (Ord. 31018)

sections.title: Off-Street Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.114. OFF-STREET LOADING.

Off-street loading must be provided as indicated on the conceptual plan. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.115. LANDSCAPING.

Landscaping must be provided in accordance with the landscape plan (Exhibit 353C). All plant material must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition at all times. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.116. SIGNS.

(a) In general. Unless otherwise provided in Subsection (b), all signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts contained in 51A-7.400.

(b) Athletic facility signs. The messages for signs facing the baseball field on the inside of the baseball outfield fence must be visually screened from Ellensberg Drive, Ridgeside Drive, Heatherbrook Drive, Inwood Road, and Willow Lane, and may not project above the height of the outfield fence. Baseball and football stadium scoreboards are permitted provided

that they do not individually exceed 300 square feet in effective area. The scoreboards may contain commercial advertising. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)

sections.title: Lighting
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.117. LIGHTING.

Lighting on the Property must comply with the lighting requirements contained in Chapter 51A. The following additional restrictions apply to all stadium lights 70 feet or more in height on the west side of the football stadium:

(1) The luminance must not exceed 0.1 footcandle at any point on the ground five feet or more inside the boundary line and five feet above ground level of an adjacent building site in a residential district.

(2) The light sources must be shielded or directed so as not to be visible from a point five feet above ground level at the boundary line of that portion of a building site located in a residential district and within 200 feet of the light source.

(3) The baseball field lighting must be adjusted so as not to produce glare that creates a traffic hazard on streets adjacent to the Property. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)

sections.title: Vehicular Access
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.118. VEHICULAR ACCESS.

No vehicular access is allowed between the Property and Willow Lane. Any amendment which would allow vehicular access between the Property and Willow Lane must comply with the zoning amendment procedures for a change in zoning district classification, and must be reflected in the conceptual plan and planned development conditions governing the Property. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)

sections.title: General Requirements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.119. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

Use of the Property must comply with all applicable federal and state laws and regulations, and with all applicable ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)

sections.title: Paving
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.120. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-353.121. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or certificate of occupancy for a use in this PD until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code,

the construction codes, and all other applicable ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 21337; 25850)
